hooks.note: Natural EXT playback-time callback, registered as 0x62b49 in both BD start flows. Input is a borrowed 24-byte six-word playback-info record, beginning with uint64 media time in 45000 ticks/second. The stock callback quantizes and updates second-level status; it is chained before starting a separate thread. No pointer into the borrowed record is retained. Prologue push.w {r3,r4,r5,r6,r7,r8,r9,r10,r11,lr} is identical in both firmware. No native timer interval or callback slot is replaced.

APL_MEDA_BDV_cb_NotifyInfo, registered through native API_SetNotifyCallback in both BD preopen flows. The caller 0x6eda8 passes one borrowed pointer; input word0 is a changed-fields mask (0x2 carries playback state in word4). Chain stock first. Nonzero notifications publish only a local epoch and nonblocking eventfd wake, never a synchronous MM request or borrowed pointer. Prologue push.w {r3,r4,r5,r6,r7,r8,r9,lr} matches both firmware.

bindings.note: Thumb API_GetMediaTime(mm_id, uint64 output). It validates id, posts synchronous native command 0x18, and returns fresh mapped PCE title-media time. Called only on the payload's own server thread.
The exact MM id validated by API_GetMediaTime; read before and after a request.
Native MM state: callback dispatcher 0x72b98 admits 2..11; the queued media-time handler 0x6cb66 additionally rejects 9 and 11. The adapter checks both conditions before and after each request.

Authoritative uint32 PCE state. Native getters 0xb50f8,0xb5270,0xb5258 distinguish state6=activeplay,7=pause,8=discSTILL. Only state7 authorizes paused waiting; other states retain active queries. Never substitute the MM readiness enum or unchanged time.

variants.note: Compared fresh stock ELFs: callback/getter/queue-wrapper control flow and ABI retain their addresses, with only absolute data immediates shifted +0xf0. The first four hook bytes are identical (2d e9 f8 4f). The getter's exact MM-id literal and native dispatcher state literal were independently disassembled for both firmware. Not tested on physical 1.85 hardware.

lifecycle: One resident server thread per apl_bdv process, started on a natural stock callback after injection. Native API calls are serialized by its existing MM worker; errors/teardown discard samples. The payload must remain resident while a native request can still be pending.
